content:
President Donald Trump railed against the incoming Democratic majority on Thursday, threatening to veto their bills until he gets what he wants.

And at least one newly elected lawmaker is ready for him.

“Do it,” Rep.-elect Fred Wellman (D-Mo.) wrote on X. “We will show this entire country how much you hate working Americans every damn day.”

Wellman, who earlier this month flipped a seat that had been held by Republicans for more than three decades, was responding to a video in which the president said he was ready to block Democrats after the party’s history-making win in this month’s midterm elections.

“Hopefully the election’s gonna bring us together,” Trump said. “We’re just gonna go veto, veto, veto, until we get legislation that’s gonna be great for everybody.”

Trump ― who has had a red “VETO” hat on his Oval Office desk ― also posted a meme of himself as “Veto Corleone” using a giant red “veto” stamp.

But Wellman dared Trump to go ahead and try once the new majority comes into office in January.

“We aren’t scared of you,” Wellman wrote. “We aren’t going to DC to play your chickenshit games anymore.”

Trump, oddly enough, also struck a more conciliatory tone on Thursday as he insisted he didn’t want to spend the next two years using his veto power. During a Q&A session with U.S. service members, the president said he hopes he can work with Democrats to “take care of a lot of different things,” including health care.

“I’m not looking to veto everything for two years and that’s not what they want either,” he said. “So I have a feeling we’re gonna have a great relationship and a lot of things are going to get done maybe more than would have gotten done the more traditional way.”
